context:
Source: DataFrame query parity proposal v3 (item T10). Hypothesis only. D4 (NULL-order policy) is recorded in dfparity-t00-owner-decisions: NULL order is fixed in implementations, not absorbed by the comparator. Project owner does NOT accept earlier reviewers' TPC-H claims.

Progress 2026-10-01: fixed and published as PR #2502 (branch fix/tpcds-null-order-and-set-ops, worktree ../BenchBox.wt-tpcds-null-semantics, head 46a6fc0ce), held, auto-merge withheld; make pr-preflight exit 0 on that head. CAUSES (TESTED, hypothesis confirmed with corrections): (1) Q15 and Q34 expression: Polars sorts NULLs first; (2) Q15 pandas: groupby drops the NULL zip group (30 rows vs 29), and Q34 pandas leaked NaN for NULL names; (3) Q38/Q87 expression: Polars join does not match NULL keys, SQL INTERSECT/EXCEPT do (Q38 1 vs 0, Q87 4809 vs 4830 at SF 0.1); pandas already correct.

CORRECTION to the NULL-order policy (important for D4 and every NULL-order item, incl. t12): the reference treats NULL as the LARGEST value. DuckDB's default_null_order is NULLS_LAST (so ascending keys put NULLs last), and the rendered SQL adds explicit NULLS FIRST to every descending key (TESTED on Q71, Q34, Q19: ORDER BY "ext_price" DESC NULLS FIRST, "c_preferred_cust_flag" DESC NULLS FIRST). The first version of this PR used nulls_last=True for every key, which is wrong for descending keys; the head above fixes it with two helpers (_sort_null_largest_expression / _sort_null_largest_pandas, a leading is_null flag per key in the key's direction) because UnifiedLazyFrame.sort only takes one global nulls_last and pandas na_position is global. Any NULL-order fix must follow this rule (ascending last, descending first), not nulls_last=True.

Evidence: full per-query probe at SF 0.1 before/after: exactly 6 cells changed, all divergent to match (Q15 and Q34 both families, Q38 and Q87 expression), no other cell changed (28 to 22 divergent); at SF 0.03 Q34 and Q87 expression changed the same way; staged gate at 0.01 unchanged (146/198, 52 empty, 0 divergent); 10 of 14 new unit cases fail without the fix (4 of them guard the descending-key rule). Note: acceptance said pandas unchanged; Q15 and Q34 pandas improved (divergent to match), no pandas regression. FLAKY CELL (relevant to t14 and t20): Q36 on the expression family at SF 0.03 diverges in some runs of identical code (40 repeats in one process: 2 divergent without these changes, 1 with them; Q36 uses none of the changed code; detail seen: Value mismatch at row 4, column 3. Original: 0, Variant: 1). A cell that flips between runs cannot be a stable gate; the classifier and promotion gate need to detect it. Remaining: hosted CI, maintainer merge, then finish.
description: Hypothesis from a prior review (not verified by me): Q15 and Q34 on the expression family put NULLs first at position 0, and Q38/Q87 (EXCEPT/INTERSECT) differ because a Polars join treats NULL keys as unequal while SQL set operations treat them as equal (pandas merge matches NaN keys and Q38/Q87 pass on pandas). Reproduce, then fix at the cause with NULL-safe set operations and explicit NULL ordering. If a case is actually parameter drift or a tie, reclassify it.
